round_summary.round_hypothesis: For ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100, simple label-preserving batch-level perturbations applied after resize/center-crop and before normalization can improve validation accuracy without meaningfully increasing epoch time, and the most useful basic direction (geometric vs photometric vs occlusion vs blur) can be identified by testing each primitive in isolation.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Diagnose which single, atomic augmentation primitive families (geometric symmetry, geometric translation, photometric brightness/contrast, additive noise, occlusion/erasing, blur) yield accuracy gains at low, interpretable strengths, and probe one strength-sensitivity axis (weak vs moderate occlusion) to calibrate future search.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Candidates are kept mostly atomic so each validation result is directly attributable to one perturbation type. All operations are conservative, label-preserving, and applied at batch level in the required placement (after resize and center crop, before normalization). Strengths are deliberately mild to avoid altering the true class, and only one primitive (random erasing) is duplicated across two strength levels because that comparison itself is a distinct diagnostic hypothesis. Mixing/cross-sample and soft-label methods (e.g., MixUp/CutMix) are excluded per constraints.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Round 0 established that cheap geometric primitives (random_affine_translate, random_horizontal_flip) are clean wins on validation_accuracy with no epoch_time penalty, that mixing methods diverge sharply (cutmix wins, mixup fails) under a confounded alpha+mechanism comparison, that occlusion (random_erasing) trades accuracy for a plausibly real time cost, and that epoch_time is noisy enough (e.g., color_jitter weak vs moderate) that secondary-metric conclusions need re-measurement before being trusted. This round tests whether (a) the geometric gains stack when combined, (b) the mixup failure is driven by alpha rather than blend mechanism, (c) erasing's accuracy gain survives at lower area/probability with less time cost, (d) the photometric strength axis has a ceiling beyond 'moderate', and (e) underexplored families (blur, structured occlusion, stochastic composites) offer new, currently-uncharted directions.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Combine targeted exploitation of the two undisputed round-0 wins (translate, flip) with controlled ablations that isolate confounded variables from round 0 (mixup alpha vs blend mechanism; erasing area/probability vs time cost), diagnostic probes that extend axes only partially explored (color_jitter strength ceiling, cutmix patch-size sensitivity), a cautious repair attempt on the one soft negative signal (gaussian_noise), and deliberate diversification into augmentation families not yet tried (gaussian blur, structured/grid occlusion, and a stochastic multi-op composite) to broaden coverage before committing further rounds to any single motif.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Because round-0 evidence is a single run per pipeline with no variance data and at least two mechanistically implausible epoch_time swings, no single motif is trusted enough to fully exploit; the candidate set therefore balances four low-risk refinements of proven motifs (translate stronger, translate+flip stack, cutmix smaller patch, lighter erasing) against three medium-risk diagnostic/ablation candidates designed to resolve specific open confounds from round 0 (mixup alpha=1.0 to isolate blend mechanism, color_jitter 'strong' arm to find the strength ceiling, low-std/low-p gaussian_noise repair) and three higher-novelty exploration candidates (gaussian blur, grid-mask occlusion, stochastic composite) chosen because the round-0 gradient covered only geometric/photometric/mixing/noise/erasing families and left frequency-domain and structured-occlusion primitives, plus automated multi-op selection, entirely untested. All candidates remain single- or dual-op batch-level, label-preserving, and placed after resize/center-crop and before normalization per constraints.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Geometric translate/flip gains have likely reached a shared ceiling where the two effects overlap rather than add (round-1: flip+translate beat translate-alone by only +0.001), so genuinely new gains this round must come from either an orthogonal geometric axis (rotation), a resolved measurement artifact (color_jitter's implausible +625% epoch_time at p=1.0), a continued strength walk on occlusion/mixing primitives that showed monotonic strength-vs-cost trends (erasing, cutmix), or a narrower/hybrid redesign of the mechanistically-failed mixup family and previously untested but plausible primitive families (structured color noise, single-axis photometric ops).
round_summary.exploration_objective: Determine whether: (1) random_affine_translate's accuracy gain saturates past 0.15 strength in isolation; (2) a new geometric axis (mild rotation) adds non-overlapping gain on top of translate rather than redundant overlap; (3) color_jitter's extreme epoch_time blowup at 'strong' settings is a probability=1.0 implementation artifact rather than a genuine strength cost, by re-running the same strong config at p=0.5; (4) the erasing strength-reduction trend (lighter config -> better acc, smaller time penalty) generalizes to grid_mask and to smaller cutmix patch ratios; (5) mixup's failure is attributable specifically to its *global* blend scope (as opposed to blending per se) by testing a patch-restricted soft-blend hybrid; and (6) new low-risk photometric/structured-noise families (PCA color augmentation, single-axis sharpness) can add value without color_jitter's timing instability or gaussian_noise's texture damage.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Selection deliberately spans modes rather than committing to one: P1 and P2 are exploit/refine-and-diversify moves on the round's strongest confirmed motif (geometric ops), testing ceiling and a genuinely new axis (rotation) rather than repeating flip+translate. P3 is a pure diagnostic isolating a flagged measurement artifact (color_jitter timing) before any further strength conclusions are drawn on that family. P4, P5, P9 are controlled ablations continuing established monotonic strength walks (cutmix patch size, erasing area/probability, and the same reduction pattern applied to grid_mask as a generalization check) to locate accuracy/cost optima rather than assuming the trend holds everywhere. P6 is a recombination/ablation of the underperforming composite sampler, isolating whether pool dilution or low op_probability caused its shortfall. P7 is a repair of the mixup family: instead of discarding global blending outright or re-tuning alpha (already ruled out as the driver), it narrows the blend's spatial scope to test the scope-vs-mechanism distinction directly. P8 and P10 are diversification into underexplored, structurally different, lower-risk families (PCA-based structured color perturbation, single-axis sharpness) chosen because the round's only two photometric/noise entries (color_jitter, gaussian_noise) both showed instability or mild harm, so the photometric/noise space remains underexplored relative to geometric and occlusion families. Overall the set balances 2 exploit/refine, 3 strength-ablation, 1 recombination-ablation, 1 mechanism-repair, and 2 diversification candidates, avoiding over-commitment to the geometric family while still respecting its strong evidence.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: Geometric batch perturbations (translate, flip, rotation) and a narrowed-pool stochastic sampler remain the strongest label-preserving levers found so far, but three open questions block further exploitation: (1) whether translate's accuracy ceiling sits precisely between 0.15 and 0.2, (2) whether the round-2 sampler win came from pool-narrowing, probability-raising, or both, and (3) whether color_jitter's persistent >250% epoch_time blowup is driven by a specific channel (hue) or is a general multi-channel cost artifact. Occlusion/mixing families (cutmix, erasing, grid_mask, patch_soft_blend) show non-monotonic strength-vs-accuracy curves that are still under-resolved between the tested endpoints. This round should mix precise refinement/ablation of the strongest motifs with diagnostic isolation of unresolved cost anomalies, while adding at least two structurally new op families to keep coverage from narrowing prematurely around geometric+cutmix.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Pin down the translate accuracy ceiling and the true driver of the sampler's history-best result via controlled single-variable ablations; isolate whether color_jitter's cost blowup is channel-specific (hue) versus strength-general; fill in the missing midpoints of the cutmix/erasing/grid_mask strength curves to locate true optima rather than just endpoints; and introduce untested geometric (perspective warp) and photometric (bit-depth quantization) families to avoid over-converging on the same three op types before their relative ranking is fully understood.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: History shows consistent, large, low-noise wins for translate/flip/sampler (multiple rounds, always positive on both metrics), so this round keeps two direct refinements of that motif (narrower translate probe, probability-only sampler ablation) as exploitation. Because round 2 confounded pool-narrowing and probability-increase in the same pipeline, and rotation only matched rather than beat flip+translate, two recombination candidates test rotation magnitude and a 3-op geometric pool separately to disentangle these effects. Color_jitter has shown a strength-linked (not probability-linked) cost blowup across two rounds with no channel-level isolation yet, so a hue-only diagnostic pipeline is included to test the leading hypothesis before the family is written off or pursued further. Cutmix, erasing, and grid_mask all show reversed or diminishing trends between two tested strength points without a midpoint measurement, so three interpolating candidates are included to map their curves rather than continue blind strength walks. Finally, two structurally new families (perspective warp, posterize/bit-depth quantization) are added at conservative settings to diversify beyond the geometric/occlusion/jitter families that have dominated all three rounds so far, and one repair candidate targets patch_soft_blend's known overhead by removing per-batch alpha randomization to test whether the cost is mechanism-inherent or implementation-inherent.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The geometric-sampler frontier (flip+translate+rotation family) is near a probability/pool ceiling around acc 0.745 rather than a strength ceiling, color_jitter's severe epoch_time blowup is driven by multi-channel joint computation rather than any single channel (hue alone was flat-cost, but brightness/contrast/saturation combinations remain untested in isolation), and several 'repaired' cheap variants (patch_soft_blend fixed-alpha, posterize) traded away too much accuracy and may have headroom to recover it without reintroducing their prior cost penalties. Round coverage so far has stayed almost entirely within geometric, photometric-jitter, and patch-occlusion/blend families; genuinely new low-risk photometric and local-warp families remain underexplored.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Close the remaining gap to history-best (acc 0.745 / epoch_time 106.60) by (1) finishing the sampler probability sweep on both the 2-op and 3-op geometric pools, (2) isolating which color_jitter channel(s) actually drive the epoch_time blowup via single- and paired-channel probes, (3) pushing the now-cheap patch_soft_blend and posterize repairs to stronger settings to test whether accuracy scales back up while cost stays low, (4) adding one repeat-run diagnostic to separate real per-setting cost from measurement noise, and (5) introducing two genuinely new, low-risk augmentation families (autocontrast, light elastic warp) plus one geometric+occlusion recombination to diversify the search beyond the three families explored so far.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: History shows geometric batch-sampler composites are the only clean, consistent double-win family (acc and epoch_time both improving), so two candidates directly continue that probability/pool exploitation with single-variable control. Color_jitter's cost anomaly is the round's most valuable unresolved diagnostic thread (hue-only refuted the p=1.0-artifact and hue-driver theories but left brightness/contrast/saturation unexamined in isolation), so two low-cost channel-isolation probes are included to pin the mechanism before any further strength tuning is attempted. Patch_soft_blend and posterize were successfully de-risked on cost last round but under-delivered on accuracy, so both get a single controlled strength increase to test whether the accuracy shortfall was a strength artifact rather than an inherent ceiling. One cutmix repeat-run at the previously anomalous 0.11 setting is included purely to address the round-3 uncertainty about cost noise versus real per-setting variance, since no repeated-run data exists anywhere in history. Two new families (autocontrast, light elastic warp) are added under diversification/risk-taking policy: both are cheap, single-mechanism, and label-preserving, giving safe exploratory coverage outside the three dominant families. Finally, a geometric+light-cutmix recombination tests whether stacking the strongest proven family with a modest occlusion component can exceed the pure-geometric ceiling, since no cross-family stack has yet been tried at conservative strength.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The geometric sampler family (flip+translate, optionally +rotation) has converged near an accuracy ceiling around 0.745 with epoch_time at or below baseline; sampler op_probability is a real, independent lever separate from pool composition (pipeline 31 showed lowering it from 0.8 to 0.6 cost -2.12% accuracy on the same pool); color_jitter's severe epoch_time blowup is not caused by hue alone (pipeline 34 was flat on cost) and is more likely a joint multi-channel computation artifact; and the two 'repaired' low-cost families (patch_soft_blend with fixed alpha, random_posterize) achieved cheap epoch_time but still trail history-best on accuracy, leaving open whether raising their strength now that overhead is controlled can close that gap. Round 4 produced zero pipeline results, so five previously-planned diagnostic threads (probability sweep, channel isolation, strength-recovery repair, cutmix repeat-run noise check, and new-family exploration) were never actually tested and remain fully open going into this round.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Re-establish measurement continuity after the empty round 4 by (1) replicating the history-best config once to obtain a same-condition variance estimate, (2) resolving the sampler probability-accuracy knee and testing whether the 3-op pool closes the residual gap to history-best at higher probability, (3) isolating a joint two-channel color_jitter perturbation to test the multi-channel-cost hypothesis left open after hue-alone showed no blowup, (4) probing whether the now-cheap fixed-alpha patch_soft_blend and posterize families can recover more accuracy at higher strength without reintroducing overhead, (5) repeating cutmix's ambiguous midpoint (0.11) to separate real cost variation from measurement noise, (6) testing a geometric+occlusion recombination that was planned but never executed, and (7) diversifying into two cheap new photometric families and one cautious new geometric family (elastic warp) to broaden coverage beyond affine transforms, given that only geometric/photometric/occlusion/mixing families have been explored so far.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: History shows strong, consistent evidence for the geometric-sampler motif (clean wins across all four completed rounds, near-ceiling accuracy with favorable or neutral epoch_time), so this round includes conservative refinements of it (probability knee-finding, 3-op probability push, an exact variance replicate) rather than abandoning it. Evidence for color_jitter and the mixing/occlusion families is mixed-to-negative but mechanistically interesting (hue-alone refuted the probability-artifact and hue-driver theories), so this round includes narrow diagnostic isolations rather than discarding the families outright. Two families (patch_soft_blend, posterize) were successfully repaired for cost but remain accuracy-uncompetitive, so this round tests whether strength can be raised now that overhead is controlled, isolating the strength-vs-recovered-overhead question. Coverage of augmentation families remains narrow (no color-inversion, no grayscale, no non-affine geometric warp tested successfully), so three diversification candidates are included at conservative strength to avoid repeating random_perspective's severe cost blowup. One recombination candidate (geometric sampler + cutmix) tests whether gains compound across families, which no prior round has directly measured. Overall the round mixes exploitation, ablation/diagnostics, repair, recombination, and diversification rather than committing to a single mode, consistent with the mixed and partially-lost (round-4) evidence base.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The accuracy ceiling (0.745, geometric 2-op sampler at op_probability=0.8) has not been exceeded in three subsequent rounds; the closest approach (3-op geometric sampler at op_probability=0.6, acc 0.7406) was never re-tested at the higher probability=0.8 that made the 2-op version win, and no run of any config has ever been repeated to establish measurement noise. Meanwhile round 5 showed that stacking a cross-family op (cutmix) after the proven sampler hurts both metrics, while three cheap new photometric families (solarize, grayscale, elastic_transform) beat baseline cheaply but stayed 4.5-7pp below the ceiling with their strength never pushed. This round should (1) close the untested probability x pool interaction directly, (2) finally obtain a variance estimate on the history-best config itself, and (3) push the cheap-but-weak families (patch_soft_blend, elastic_transform, and a compatible photometric recombination) toward the ceiling under controlled, single-variable changes.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Resolve the outstanding probability/pool interaction for the geometric sampler family (does 3-op pool at op_probability=0.8 beat or match the 2-op history-best?), obtain a same-condition noise estimate for the history-best pipeline for the first time, isolate which color_jitter channel (brightness, tested here, vs the already-cleared hue) drives its severe epoch_time blowup, and probe whether previously cost-repaired but accuracy-weak families (patch_soft_blend, elastic_transform) can be strengthened without reintroducing cost penalties. In parallel, diversify with an unexplored cheap photometric family (autocontrast) and test a same-family-compatible recombination (geometric sampler + solarize) as a lower-risk alternative to the failed geometric+cutmix stack.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: History shows the geometric sampler family is the only motif with a reproducible clean-win profile across rounds, so one candidate exploits it directly at the untested probability=0.8/3-op combination, and a second isolates the probability lever alone at an intermediate value (0.7) to map the knee more precisely. Because no round has ever repeated an identical configuration, one candidate is a pure replicate of the history-best pipeline to finally quantify run-to-run noise, which the round conclusions have flagged as a blocking uncertainty six times. The color_jitter cost mystery remains only half-diagnosed (hue cleared, other channels untested), so a brightness-only isolation is included. The two 'cost was fixed but accuracy stayed low' families (patch_soft_blend, elastic_transform) get controlled strength increases to test whether their accuracy floor can rise while the cost fix holds. Diversification continues cautiously with autocontrast (planned twice, never run). Recombination is retried with a same-scope-compatible cheap op (solarize) instead of the cross-sample op (cutmix) that failed twice, both as a sequential stack and as a sampler-pool member, to separate composition strategy from op choice. This mix balances exploitation of the strongest known motif, unresolved diagnostics, narrow repair/strengthening, and genuinely new coverage, while avoiding over-committing further budget to occlusion/mixing families (erasing, grid_mask, cutmix, mixup) that have already been extensively strength-walked with diminishing or negative returns.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The geometric random_op_sampler (flip+translate, op_probability=0.8) remains the strongest known configuration, but round 6's exact replicate (0.7278/111.16s vs recorded 0.745/106.60s) revealed a noise band (~1.7pp accuracy, ~4.5s time) large enough to make most recent inter-round deltas non-attributable; simultaneously, probability appears to interact with pool size (3-op pool peaked near p=0.6-0.7, not p=0.8 like the 2-op pool), color_jitter's cost blowup survives single-channel isolation (hue, brightness both flat) implicating a joint multi-channel interaction, and cross-family recombination (cutmix, solarize) consistently dilutes rather than compounds the geometric ceiling regardless of stacking order tried so far.
round_summary.exploration_objective: (1) Re-measure the history-best config to build a second noise data point before trusting small deltas; (2) continue mapping the probability x pool-size interaction on the 3-op geometric pool at an untested intermediate probability; (3) finish the color_jitter single-channel isolation sweep (contrast, saturation) to pin down whether the cost blowup is channel-specific or requires multi-channel joint computation; (4) test a reordered geometric-then-mixing vs mixing-then-geometric composition for cutmix to see if operation order (not just stacking style) explains its post-hoc accuracy/cost penalty; (5) isolate patch_soft_blend's blend-strength axis separately from its area axis, since area increase alone failed to recover accuracy; (6) exploit the cheap, promising solarize family by strengthening it inside pool-integration (the composition style that already beat sequential stacking); (7) diversify into an untested geometric axis (scale/zoom) and an untested composition mechanism (single-op-per-batch RandAugment-style selection), plus one narrow-risk new photometric family (channel permutation) to keep coverage broad given how many recent narrow-strength probes have plateaued.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: History is strong and consistent for the geometric family but its exact magnitude is now known to be noisy, so this round allocates one slot purely to variance re-estimation (repair/diagnostic) rather than exploitation. Because probability and pool-size clearly interact (2-op optimum near 0.8, 3-op optimum apparently lower), one candidate fills the untested 0.7 gap on the 3-op pool rather than re-testing known points. Color_jitter's cost mechanism is still unresolved after two channels cleared, so the remaining two channels are tested individually rather than abandoning the family outright, per the policy of isolating failing components instead of discarding them. Cutmix and patch_soft_blend both have real positive standalone histories that failed only in specific recombination/scaling contexts, so both get a narrowly redesigned retry (reordering, alpha-isolation) rather than repetition of the failed variant or outright removal. One exploitation candidate refines the best cheap diversification finding (solarize) using the composition style already shown superior. Two candidates are genuinely novel (scale/zoom axis, single-op-per-batch selection mechanism) to guard against over-fitting to the flip+translate+sampler motif, and one low-probability, safeguarded new photometric op (channel permutation) provides a higher-novelty, lower-commitment diversification probe consistent with keeping risk levels varied across the round.

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The geometric-sampler accuracy ceiling (~0.72-0.745, achieved by 2-op and 3-op flip/translate/rotation pools) sits inside a measurement noise band that is now empirically larger than most of the inter-pipeline deltas reported across rounds 0-7 (~2.2pp accuracy / ~9.3s epoch_time across three nominal replicates of the identical 2-op config). Within that band, two structurally distinct signals still look attributable and worth extending: (1) pool-integration recombination beats sequential stacking for adding a secondary op (solarize-in-pool: +0.0156 acc for +1.1s vs the matched 2-op baseline; cutmix-as-sequential-stack has failed in every prior attempt including a reorder test that ruled out ordering as the cause), and (2) color_jitter's severe epoch_time blowup survives at every single isolated channel (hue, brightness, contrast, saturation all individually fast) but has never been tested with two channels active simultaneously, leaving a joint-interaction mechanism unconfirmed.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Increase confidence in the current best region via targeted replication, extend the proven pool-integration composition pattern to two more single-axis candidates (scale, cutmix) that previously only succeeded or failed under different compositions, run the first direct joint-channel color_jitter cost diagnostic, repair-check the unexplained patch_soft_blend alpha=0.3 cost spike via exact replicate, ablate ops_per_batch separately from op_probability to disentangle the pool-size x probability interaction seen across rounds 6-7, and add one new conservatively-tuned photometric family to keep family coverage broad.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Given seven rounds of partially-supported hypotheses, an empty round, and a just-measured noise band wider than most claimed effects, this round deliberately balances confirmation over pure exploitation: two pipelines are near-exact replicates of ambiguous prior results (top 3-op pool config; anomalous patch_soft_blend cost spike) to convert single-run deltas into attributable signals. Three pipelines extend the one clearly-attributable recombination pattern from history (pool-integration beating stacking) to scale, a higher-probability-matched solarize variant, and a repaired cutmix-as-pool-member design, since the failure mode for cutmix (misalignment/dilution under sequential stacking) has never been tested under the composition style that rescued solarize. One higher-risk pipeline (4-op combined pool) tests whether the two independently-positive recombination adds compound or dilute together, consistent with round 6-7's finding that larger pools need lower probability. One diagnostic isolates ops_per_batch from op_probability, a confound flagged but never separately tested. One diagnostic directly tests the joint-channel color_jitter cost hypothesis that four single-channel isolations left unresolved. One diversification pipeline (histogram equalization) adds a new, conservatively-tuned photometric family, since the cheap single-axis photometric ops tested so far (solarize, sharpness, posterize) have been safe but never included this specific mechanism. No pipeline repeats an exact prior parameterization except the two explicit replication probes, and no strategy family is discarded outright despite negative history (cutmix, color_jitter, patch_soft_blend all get narrowly-scoped, better-controlled follow-ups rather than exclusion).

round_summary.round_hypothesis: The project has established two firm facts and one major methodological correction: (1) label-preserving geometric batch ops (flip, translate, scale, and to a lesser extent rotation) form a robust high-accuracy/low-cost cluster whose members are roughly interchangeable, and (2) the measured noise band for this cluster (~2-2.5pp accuracy across identical-config replicates) is wide enough that most 'improvements' claimed in rounds 5-8 over the 0.745 ceiling are not distinguishable from noise. Cross-family recombination (cutmix, solarize, patch_soft_blend) has repeatedly produced ambiguous or negative results when stacked or pooled at reduced per-op probability, plausibly because (a) cutmix/mixup-style cross-sample mixing introduces content that is only approximately consistent with the retained hard label, and (b) adding pool members while holding ops_per_batch constant dilutes each member's effective application rate. This round tests whether a same-class-constrained patch operation can capture cutmix's regularization benefit without the label-content mismatch, whether raising ops_per_batch compensates for pool dilution, and continues isolating two open cost mechanisms (color_jitter's still-unexplained multi-channel blowup, random_equalize's surprising cost blowup) rather than assuming either is settled.
round_summary.exploration_objective: Reduce noise-driven false conclusions by replicating the round's most promising but unreplicated result (cutmix-in-pool) before trusting it; test one direct repair of the dilution problem (raise ops_per_batch for a 4-op pool) and one direct repair of cutmix's hypothesized content-mismatch problem (same-class patch source); isolate flip's marginal contribution via a flip-free geometric pool; extend the color_jitter channel-isolation thread to three simultaneous channels; probe random_equalize's and patch_soft_blend's cost mechanisms with narrower/lower-strength variants rather than abandoning either family outright; and add one genuinely new cheap geometric family (shear) plus one exploitation of an underexplored cheap lead (stronger posterize) to keep the candidate set from over-concentrating on the existing geometric-sampler motif.
round_summary.strategy_selection_rationale: Given the strong-but-noisy evidence for the geometric-sampler motif, roughly a third of the candidates directly test or refine it (verification replicate, scale-probability refinement, flip-ablation simplification) rather than assuming its exact past numbers are reliable. Because cross-family recombination has been the most inconsistent thread across rounds 5-8, this round allocates deliberate diagnostic and repair candidates to it (same-class cutmix, ops_per_batch-compensated 4-op pool) instead of either repeating the same stacking pattern or discarding cross-sample mixing entirely. Two candidates continue unresolved cost-mechanism investigations (color_jitter 3-channel joint test, random_equalize low-probability isolation) because both ops showed surprising, unexplained epoch_time behavior that a single data point cannot yet explain. One candidate narrows patch_soft_blend's patch area while holding its only known-safe alpha fixed, isolating area as the remaining free variable given two consistent rounds of cost-blowup evidence at other settings. Finally, one new affine family (shear) and one strength-push on an underexplored cheap op (posterize) preserve diversification so the candidate set is not entirely composed of parameter refinements of the existing best motif.
